newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara aiming to boost insurance sector.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara aiming to boost insurance sector.

text.p: The Malaysian central bank aims to make the insurance industry a key component of the financial services sector, The Star newspaper quoted Bank Negara Governor Ahmad Mohamad Don as saying on Tuesday.
Ahmad said in an interview more emphasis would be placed on measures to encourage insurers to improve their capital strength so that they could assume greater risks and expand operations.

"Our new stance is to create an environment that rewards insurers who are fully committed in terms of upgrading their technical expertise, capital strength and hence, capacity to handle greater business risks," he was quoted as saying.
He said by 2000 there should be a core of 10 to 15 well-capitalised and well-managed insurers capable of competing in the open market.
Assets of the insurance industry should account for at least five percent of total assets of the financial system, and half of all Malaysians should hold a life policy, Ahmad said.

"For the future, there will be progressive liberalisation of rules to allow room for the better-capitalised and more well-managed insurers to expand their business base and help drive the market towards greater efficiency and competitiveness," he said.
